backlog.spec: Provide jac for the objective (-1 on radii, 0 on centres) and an analytic constraint Jacobian (pairwise distance gradients, wall constraints, r>=0) as a dense array to minimize. This avoids finite differences (~129 variables), giving many more restarts/iterations in 30 s.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobian for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Set MAX_ITER=500 and ftol=1e-10 in SLSQP options so each start converges fully. Combined with fewer restarts this may reach better local optima.
backlog.title: Raise MAX_ITER to 500 with convergence tol

backlog.spec: After a few random starts, spend the remaining time perturbing the best packing (jitter centres by sd ~0.03, shrink radii by half, or relocate the 1-3 smallest circles to random positions) and re-running SLSQP from there. Keep the result if better.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the best solution

backlog.spec: Run short SLSQP (maxiter 60) from many random starts for 50% of time, then fully polish (maxiter 400) the top 3 candidates by sum of radii in the remaining time.
backlog.title: Two-phase: restarts then polish top-k

backlog.spec: Initialise centres on a jittered hexagonal/staggered lattice with rows of 5-6 (about 32 sites, random row-count choice) plus noise sd 0.02, with radii of 0.08. Good packings are near-lattice.
backlog.title: Hex-grid perturbed initialisation

backlog.spec: Initialise radii randomly from uniform(0.03,0.15) instead of constant 0.05, so that the optimiser sees diverse size distributions (large and small circles).
backlog.title: Mixed-size initial radii

backlog.spec: Increase TIME_FRACTION to 0.92 after making the loop check the remaining time against an estimated per-start duration so as not to exceed the limit. Gives more search with little risk.
backlog.title: Use TIME_FRACTION 0.92

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, fix the centres and solve an LP with scipy linprog (maximise sum r subject to r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=wall distance, r>=0) and subtract 1e-12. This gives the best valid radii for the centres, replacing the greedy shrink.
backlog.title: Better repair via exact LP radii

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run a cheap L-BFGS-B on a smooth overlap-penalty energy with gradually increasing radii, from random centres, to produce a feasible-ish start. Then run SLSQP from that.
backlog.title: Penalty-based pre-relaxation

backlog.spec: Set INIT_LOW to 0.03 so centres cover the whole square, including the boundaries where large-radius packings place circles.
backlog.title: Smaller init range INIT_LOW=0.03

backlog.spec: In each SLSQP run only include pairs within a distance of 0.35 at the start, then re-run with the full set once for validation. Fewer constraints give a faster QP step.
backlog.title: Prune the pair constraints

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP in rounds of 50 iterations; between rounds, rebuild the active pair list (pairs with d-r_i-r_j<0.1) and warm-start from the previous solution. Faster per-iteration cost.
backlog.title: Sequential SLSQP with constraint-set refresh

backlog.spec: Polish the best final solution with trust-constr or SLSQP with tight tolerance (ftol 1e-14) for the remaining 10% of time, then LP-repair.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish

backlog.spec: From the best packing, pick the smallest circle and a random large gap point (largest empty circle found by sampling 2000 points), move the circle there with a small radius, re-optimise with SLSQP. Accept on improvement.
backlog.title: Swap-move local search

backlog.spec: For half of the restarts, generate 16 random circles and mirror them about x=0.5 or the diagonal to give 32 as the starting point, then optimise without the symmetry constraint.
backlog.title: Symmetric initialisation

backlog.spec: Keep a pool of the 5 best packings; create a new start by taking the circles of one with x<t and the circles of another with x>=t (choose t so the count is 32, adjusting by random removals/additions), then SLSQP.
backlog.title: Elite pool crossover

backlog.spec: In basin-hopping from the best solution, decrease the perturbation sd linearly from 0.06 to 0.005 over the time budget.
backlog.title: Annealed perturbation scale

backlog.spec: Set INIT_RADIUS to 0.02 (growth from tiny circles gives less initial overlap and fewer stuck contacts).
backlog.title: Start radii from small value 0.02

backlog.spec: Write pair constraints as the squared distance minus (ri+rj)^2 (smooth at zero distance, cheaper without sqrt) with an analytic Jacobian. This improves conditioning at the start when centres coincide.
backlog.title: Constraint in squared form

backlog.spec: Pass bounds=[(0,1)]*2n+[(0,0.5)]*n to SLSQP instead of the r constraints and drop the wall constraints on centres to bounds on centres [0,1]. This reduces the constraint count.
backlog.title: Remove r>=0 constraints via bounds

backlog.spec: Make _repair loop until no overlap remains (up to 500 iterations) instead of 50, and verify the final overlap <=0 so that residual overlaps never get returned.
backlog.title: Vectorised repair with best LP fallback

backlog.spec: Run every start for just 40 iterations, and continue to 300 iterations only if the sum of the radii is within 3% of the best-so-far screening value. Saves time on bad starts.
backlog.title: Multi-start screening by early objective

backlog.spec: Init about 14 circles around the boundary ring (perimeter, equal spacing, radius 0.07) and 18 interior ones from a random jitter. Known good packings have boundary circles.
backlog.title: Ring+interior init

backlog.spec: From the best solution, remove the k=2-4 smallest circles, re-sample their centres uniformly with radius 0.01, and run SLSQP on all. Repeat until time is out.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert smallest k

backlog.spec: Perturb the best centres with noise scaled by 0.05/(r_i/mean r), so small circles move more, and re-run SLSQP using the best radii times 0.8 as the start.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted random jitter restarts

backlog.spec: Cache the iu indices outside _solve_once (compute once per n) and precompute the wall-index arrays. Reduces per-call overhead and so allows more restarts.
backlog.title: Pair-pruned neighbour Jacobian sparse via SLSQP warm start

backlog.spec: Create the starts by 10 Lloyd iterations of random points in the square (approximated with a 100x100 grid sample), giving evenly spread centres. Set radii 0.07.
backlog.title: Lloyd relaxation init

backlog.spec: Track the maximum single-start duration, and stop the loop when the remaining time is less than 1.5x that, so that TIME_FRACTION can rise to 0.95 safely.
backlog.title: Time-aware loop guard

backlog.spec: Reduce SHRINK to 2e-11 after verifying with an exact check that the repaired packing has overlaps <=1e-12, since the tolerance is 1e-10. Gains ~3e-8 per circle; a tiny effect but trivial.
backlog.title: Final tiny shrink SHRINK 1e-12

backlog.spec: Supply jac= to SLSQP for the objective (gradient is -1 on radius entries, 0 on centres) and a constraint Jacobian function. For pair constraints d_ij = |ci-cj| - ri - rj, row k has (ci-cj)/dist on ci, the negative of that on cj, and -1 on ri and rj. Boundary rows c_x - r etc. have +/-1 entries, and the r>=0 rows have 1. Build the dense Jacobian with numpy fancy indexing. This removes finite-difference cost (about 97 evaluations per gradient) so many more restarts fit in 30 s. Guard dist with a 1e-12 floor.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobian for constraints and objective

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP result from a pool member, make a new start: take the best pool packing, delete the k=2 or 3 circles with the smallest radii, and re-place each at a random point chosen as the best of 200 random candidates, scored by the max distance to the nearest other circle edge (distance to the centres minus their radii, and the wall distance). Give each reinserted circle a radius of 0.02. Run SLSQP from this start. Use this for 30% of restarts in place of the crossover.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert smallest circles into largest holes

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run about 50 steps of L-BFGS-B on the penalised objective -sum(r) + mu*sum(max(0, overlap)^2) + mu*wall violations squared, with mu=50 and an analytic gradient, with centres in [0,1] and r in [0,0.3] as bounds. Then run SLSQP from the result with a lower MAX_ITER of 100. This gives SLSQP feasible-ish, well-spread starts and should cut its iterations.
backlog.title: Penalty pre-relaxation before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace random initialisation for non-crossover starts with a jittered hex-like grid. Use rows of 6,5,6,5,6,4 or similar totalling 32, with a row spacing of about 1/6 and a random jitter of sd 0.02. Set radii to uniform random values in [0.04,0.11]. Randomly permute which circles get large radii. This starts near the dense known structure rather than from uniform noise.
backlog.title: Mixed-size initial radii with hex-grid centres

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP in two stages. Stage one: a quick solve with all constraints at MAX_ITER=60. Stage two: keep only pair constraints with d_ij < 0.15 at the stage-one solution, and re-solve to convergence with those constraints (about 100 pairs instead of 496). Then check all pairs and, if any are violated, add them and rerun. SLSQP cost scales with the number of constraints, so this speeds up each restart a lot.
backlog.title: Sparse neighbour-only constraints with active-set refresh

backlog.spec: Replace _repair with a scipy linprog (HiGHS) that, for fixed centres, maximises sum(r) subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij - 1e-12 for all pairs, r_i <= wall distance, r>=0. Run it on every SLSQP result so that the pool compares true optimal radii for given centres. Fall back to the old repair if the LP fails. It also recovers radius lost by the greedy shrink.
backlog.title: Exact LP radius repair

backlog.spec: For 25% of fresh starts, generate 16 random circles in the left half (x<0.5), mirror them across x=0.5 to make 32, and perturb all by a small noise of sd 0.005. Radii start at 0.05. SLSQP then breaks the symmetry as needed. This explores a structured subspace where good packings often lie, and halves the effective randomness.
backlog.title: Symmetric start via mirrored half-packing

backlog.spec: For pool-based restarts, replace the current perturbation with a move that picks one circle at random weighted by 1/radius (so small circles are favoured), moves it to a uniform random position, sets its radius to 0.01, and also jitters all other centres with sd 0.01. Run SLSQP from it. Accept the result into the pool only if its sum beats the worst pool member. This is a targeted large move rather than the Gaussian jitter that failed.
backlog.title: Large-radius-biased relocation moves

backlog.spec: Increase the pool to 12 and reject a new packing from entering the pool if its sorted radius vector is within 1e-3 in L2 norm of an existing member (a duplicate). Pick crossover parents uniformly from the pool. This keeps diversity so crossover mixes different structures instead of copies of one basin.
backlog.title: Larger pool with diversity filter

backlog.spec: Run each SLSQP in two phases: first optimise with the objective -sum(r) while capping r<=0.09 through bounds, which forces a more uniform spread, for 60 iterations. Then drop the cap (bounds r<=0.5) and continue for up to 200 iterations from that point. Pass bounds to minimize for the centres in [0,1] and remove the r>=0 constraints. The cap acts as a regulariser that avoids early big-circle lock-in.
backlog.title: Two-phase objective: shrunken radii warm start

backlog.spec: Supply analytic jac for both the objective (gradient -1 on radii, 0 on centres) and the constraint vector in _solve_once. Build the constraint Jacobian as a dense matrix: for each pair k=(i,j), d/dc_i=(ci-cj)/dist, d/dc_j=-that, d/dr_i=d/dr_j=-1; wall rows have +-1 on the coordinate and -1 on r; r>=0 rows are identity. Use np.maximum(dist,1e-12). Pass jac= to minimize and to the constraint dict. This removes finite-difference cost (about 96 evaluations per Jacobian) so many more restarts fit in the time budget.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Combine slots 8 and 9. Pool size 12; skip a new packing if its sorted radius vector is within 1e-3 L2 of one already in the pool. Fresh (non-crossover) starts use a staggered hex-like lattice with random row count 5-7, jittered by sd 0.02 and initial radius 0.05. Keep the rest of the loop unchanged. The spec is a single combined change.
backlog.title: Replicate pool of 12 with diversity filter plus lattice starts

backlog.spec: After the loop, with the best centres fixed, solve an LP with scipy.optimize.linprog (highs) maximising sum r subject to r_i+r_j <= d_ij, r_i <= wall distance, r>=0. Then subtract SHRINK 1e-9 from the radii and verify with the exact check. Replace the best packing only if its sum is larger. Also apply this LP to every candidate in place of _repair, so the pool ranks packings by their true value.
backlog.title: Exact LP radius re-optimisation of final packing

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, draw initial radii from a log-uniform distribution on [0.02, 0.12] rather than a constant 0.05, and assign centres by sorting so that the larger radii are placed first with rejection sampling to limit overlap (up to 20 tries each). This gives SLSQP starts that already have size diversity, as optimal packings have varied radii.
backlog.title: Mixed-size random initial radii

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP start, run 30-50 steps of gradient descent on the energy -sum(r) + mu*sum(max(0, r_i+r_j-d_ij)^2) + mu*wall violations squared, with mu rising from 10 to 1000 (use vectorised numpy and an analytic gradient). Use the result as the SLSQP x0. This moves the random starts to near-feasible configurations so SLSQP needs fewer iterations and lands in better basins.
backlog.title: Penalty-based pre-relaxation

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, run SLSQP with only the pair constraints with centre distance < 2.5*max(r)+0.1 at the starting point, about 150 pairs instead of 496. After it finishes, check all pairs. If any are violated, rebuild the pair set and rerun from the result (max 3 rounds). This shrinks the QP size so that each run is much faster and more restarts fit.
backlog.title: Neighbour-only constraints with refresh

backlog.spec: Perturbation move: take the best pool packing, remove the single smallest circle, and put it at the point among 2000 random samples that maximises the distance to the nearest circle surface and the walls (largest hole). Give it that radius, then run SLSQP. Use this move for 30% of restarts, with the others unchanged. Differs from slot 10 in that it removes only one circle and uses a hole search instead of random resampling.
backlog.title: Swap and relocate smallest circle into largest hole

backlog.spec: For half of the fresh starts, generate 16 random circles in the left half x<0.5, then mirror them across x=0.5 to make 32 circles, and add a small jitter of sd 0.005 to break exact symmetry. Run SLSQP from there. Symmetric structures are often near-optimal in square packings, and this halves the effective search dimension.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric half packing start

backlog.spec: Stage 1: solve SLSQP with the objective -sum(r) but with an added bound r<=0.09 and maxiter 80. Stage 2: remove the bound and continue to maxiter 200 from the stage 1 result. The cap prevents early dominance by a few big circles and favours balanced layouts. Compare with the plain run through the pool as usual.
backlog.title: Two-stage radius inflation schedule

backlog.spec: Replace the vertical-cut crossover with a random-angle line cut: pick a random direction and offset through the centre area, take circles on one side from parent A and the other side from parent B. Delete any circle in B's part whose centre lies within 0.5 of the sum of radii of an A circle, then refill to n with the largest-hole search. Give the child small radii (0.8x) before SLSQP so that it starts feasible.
backlog.title: Pool crossover on spatial region with local repair

backlog.spec: Supply analytic gradients to SLSQP. Pass jac=lambda v: concat(zeros(2n), -ones(n)) for the objective. For the constraints, pass a jac function returning the dense matrix: for pair k=(i,j) with d=||ci-cj||, the row has (ci-cj)/d at ci's two columns, -(ci-cj)/d at cj's two columns, and -1 at r_i and r_j. Use +1/-1 entries for the wall constraints and +1 for r>=0. Guard d with max(d,1e-12). Precompute iu once. This removes finite-difference cost (about 100 times per iteration) so many more restarts fit in 30 s. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Re-adopt slot 11: for fresh random starts, relax centres with L-BFGS-B on a smooth overlap-penalty energy (sum of squared overlaps of circles with fixed radii plus wall violations) before SLSQP. Additionally combine with slot 9: pool size 12, and skip a new packing if its sorted radius vector is within 1e-3 L2 of an existing pool member. Crossover and perturbation starts are drawn from the pool as before.
backlog.title: Penalty-energy relaxation of fresh starts, with pool of 12 diverse

backlog.spec: After the restart loop, take the best centres and solve the LP: maximise sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs, r_i <= wall distance, r_i >= 0, using scipy.optimize.linprog (highs). Subtract 1e-12 from the radii, then run the existing repair as a safety check. Keep the result if its sum is larger than the repaired SLSQP result. This recovers slack lost by SLSQP tolerance and the 1e-9 shrink.
backlog.title: Exact LP radius re-optimisation of final packing

backlog.spec: For 30% of restarts, take a random pool packing and swap the radii of two circles of clearly different radius (ratio over 1.3) that are within 0.3 of each other, keeping centres. Run SLSQP from this start with maxiter 200. This explores permutations of big and small circles, a change that continuous local optimisation cannot reach. Do not apply large jitter.
backlog.title: Swap-radius moves between neighbours in pool members

backlog.spec: For 25% of fresh starts, generate 16 random circles in the left half (x<0.5) with radius 0.06, and mirror them about x=0.5 to get 32 circles. Run SLSQP on the full 32-circle problem from this symmetric start; SLSQP will break symmetry if that is better. Other fresh starts stay random.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric half-packing starts

backlog.spec: Combine slot 8 and slot 11. A fresh start has a staggered hex-like lattice with random row count 5-7, where the circle count is trimmed or padded to 32 and the centres get Gaussian noise sd 0.02. Then relax with the L-BFGS-B penalty energy, then SLSQP. Use this for 50% of fresh starts and uniform-random starts for the rest.
backlog.title: Lattice starts plus penalty relaxation

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP in two stages for every start. Stage 1: maxiter 50 with constraint d_ij >= (r_i + r_j)*1.05 and wall margins scaled likewise, so the packing keeps slack and centres spread. Stage 2: the true constraints, maxiter 200, from the stage 1 result. Test whether the looser start reaches better basins.
backlog.title: Two-stage inflation with shrunken radii

backlog.spec: Generate 8 fresh starts at a time. Relax each with L-BFGS-B on the overlap-penalty energy with radii fixed at 0.09. Rank them by the total sum of radii found from a quick LP on the relaxed centres. Run SLSQP only on the top 2 of the 8. This spends the time on promising basins.
backlog.title: Batch of cheap starts, then promote best by penalty energy

backlog.spec: Use 50% of the time for diverse restarts as in the incumbent. For the remaining time, repeatedly pick the best 3 pool packings, multiply each radius by a random factor in [0.8,1.0] and keep the centres unchanged (no centre jitter), and run SLSQP with maxiter 150. Accept the result into the pool if it is better than the worst member. This uses a different perturbation type from the failed Gaussian centre jitter.
backlog.title: Adaptive time split with restart from best, small jitter on radii only

backlog.spec: Supply jac for the objective (-1 on radius entries, 0 on centres) and a vectorised analytic Jacobian for cons(v). For pair constraints: row k has d/dc_i = (ci-cj)/dist, d/dc_j = -(ci-cj)/dist, d/dr_i = d/dr_j = -1. Wall rows: c_x - r gives +1 on x_i and -1 on r_i, etc. The r>=0 rows are identity. Build with a dense zero matrix and fancy indexing. This should make each SLSQP run several times faster, so more restarts fit in the time budget. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobian for SLSQP constraints

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, run SLSQP in rounds of at most 3. In each round include only pair constraints for pairs whose centre distance at the current x is under r_i+r_j+0.25, plus all wall constraints. After each round, check all pairs and stop if none is violated by more than 1e-9; otherwise recompute the set and warm start again. This cuts the constraint count from ~496 to ~150 and speeds each iteration. Use the freed time for more restarts.
backlog.title: Neighbour-only constraints with refresh

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, place centres on a 6-row staggered hex-like grid (rows alternate 5 and 6 circles, trimmed to 32) with jitter sd 0.03. Give each circle a random radius from a bimodal mix (50% 0.06, 50% 0.11), randomly assigned. The unequal radii help SLSQP find mixed-size optima rather than uniform ones. Keep pool crossover.
backlog.title: Mixed-size initial radii with hex-grid centres

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, stage 1 solves with radii variables bounded above by 0.08 (use bounds) for 60 iterations to spread the centres evenly. Stage 2 removes the cap and continues for MAX_ITER from the stage 1 solution. This acts as a regulariser that prevents early large circles from locking the topology.
backlog.title: Two-stage inflation with shrunken radii

backlog.spec: Generate a batch of 40 random starts. Relax each with 30 L-BFGS-B steps on the overlap penalty energy, then compute the final energy plus -sum(r) score. Run full SLSQP only on the best 5 of the batch. Repeat the batch until the time is used, and feed the results into the pool as before. This spends little time on bad basins.
backlog.title: Batch of cheap starts promoted by penalty energy

backlog.spec: Replace the fresh starts in the second half of the time with this: take the best pool packing, multiply all radii by 0.7, add centre noise with sd drawn log-uniformly from [0.005, 0.04], and run SLSQP. Accept the result into the pool by the usual rule. The shrink makes the start feasible, so SLSQP reoptimises local structure instead of starting from a random point. Keep the first half as random restarts.
backlog.title: Annealed restart-from-best with shrink-and-regrow

backlog.spec: Re-implement slot 11: for fresh random starts (not crossover), before SLSQP, relax the centres with L-BFGS-B (analytic gradient) on a smooth energy: sum of squared pairwise overlaps max(0, r_i+r_j-d_ij)^2 plus squared wall violations max(0, r_i-c)^2, with radii fixed at a random mix around 0.09, then run SLSQP from the relaxed state. Keep the rest of the file unchanged (pool of 5, 70% crossover). Purpose: confirm the replicated -2.9396 as a base.
backlog.title: Re-adopt penalty-energy L-BFGS-B relaxation of fresh starts (slot 11) with pool of 5

backlog.spec: On top of the penalty-energy L-BFGS-B relaxation of fresh starts (relax centres with radii fixed near 0.09, then SLSQP), grow the pool to 12 and reject new packings whose sorted radius vector is within 1e-3 L2 of any pool member. Crossover and perturbed starts pick parents uniformly from the pool. Combines the two best-replicated signals.
backlog.title: Slot 11 relaxation plus diverse pool of 12

backlog.spec: In the penalty-energy relaxation of fresh starts, draw per-circle target radii from a uniform [0.05, 0.13] distribution rescaled so that sum of pi r^2 is about 0.8, relax centres with L-BFGS-B, then start SLSQP with those radii times 0.8. This gives mixed-size basins consistent with the best known packings.
backlog.title: Penalty relaxation with random radius targets in a size-mixed band

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed-radius penalty relaxation by a sequence of 4 L-BFGS-B solves in which the radii scale factor goes 0.6, 0.8, 0.95, 1.05 times target radii, with centres warm-started between stages. Then run SLSQP with radii at 0.9 of final scale. Mimics a Lubachevsky-Stillinger-like compression to find denser basins.
backlog.title: Annealed penalty-energy with growing radii (inflation)

backlog.spec: Instead of fixed radii, run L-BFGS-B on variables (c, r) with energy -sum(r) + mu * (overlap^2 + wall^2), with mu increased through 10, 100, 1000 over three stages. Use the result as the SLSQP start. Gradients analytic and vectorised over pairs. Applies to fresh starts only.
backlog.title: Joint centre and radius penalty optimisation with sum-of-radii reward

backlog.spec: After the loop, fix the best centres and solve a linear program with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS) maximising sum(r) subject to r_i+r_j <= d_ij - 1e-12, r_i <= wall distances. Use the result if it is valid and bigger than the repaired radii, after a final validity check with the harness tolerance. Only done once, at the end, using the final 5% of time.
backlog.title: Final exact LP radius re-optimisation of the best packing

backlog.spec: For 30% of fresh starts, sample 16 circle centres in the left half x<0.5 (relaxed by penalty energy against each other and the wall x=0.5 mirrored), mirror them to the right half to get 32 circles, then run unconstrained SLSQP from there so symmetry may break. Many best-known packings are near-symmetric.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric half-packing starts

backlog.spec: Per restart round, generate 20 random starts, relax each with 30 L-BFGS-B steps of the penalty energy, and give SLSQP only the one with the lowest final energy (or the highest sum of radii after relaxation with radii as variables). This spends cheap compute to raise the quality of the SLSQP starts.
backlog.title: Batch screening of many cheap relaxed starts by penalty energy

backlog.spec: Replace the vertical-cut crossover by a random cut along a random line (angle uniform) between two pool parents. Take circles on one side from parent A and the other side from B, fix the count to 32 by removing the smallest overlappers or adding circles at random positions, run 30 steps of penalty-energy L-BFGS-B to remove overlap, then SLSQP. Keeps the pool of 5.
backlog.title: Region-swap crossover with penalty repair

backlog.spec: Combine the replicated winners: fresh starts are 50% noisy staggered lattice, 50% uniform random, each relaxed with L-BFGS-B on a smooth squared overlap/wall penalty energy (as in slots 11 and 32) before SLSQP. Also use a pool of 12 with a 1e-3 L2 sorted-radius diversity filter (slots 9/18). Keep crossover at 70% once the pool has 2. No other changes.
backlog.title: Penalty relaxation + pool of 12 diverse + lattice base

backlog.spec: Replace the single penalty relaxation with a continuation: set target radii to 0.04, run L-BFGS-B on the squared overlap/wall penalty over centres only, then raise the targets by a factor of 1.15 per stage up to about 0.095 (6 stages, 30 iterations each), starting each stage from the previous centres. Then give the centres and the final target radii to SLSQP. This acts like a Lubachevsky-Stillinger compression and should give denser basins.
backlog.title: Annealed inflating penalty relaxation

backlog.spec: In the penalty relaxation for fresh starts, draw target radii per circle from a bimodal mix: 8 to 12 circles at 0.11-0.14 and the rest at 0.06-0.09, assigned at random. Relax the centres with L-BFGS-B against these targets, then start SLSQP with the targeted radii shrunk by 0.9. Best known packings of 32 circles have mixed sizes, so this seeds that structure.
backlog.title: Size-mixed target radii in relaxation

backlog.spec: After the loop, take the top 3 pool members. Alternate 3 times: (a) a HiGHS LP for fixed centres maximising sum r under linear constraints r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=wall distances; (b) SLSQP for 100 iterations from those radii. Finish with the greedy repair on the best result. Reserve 10% of the time for this. Slots 21 and 34 tried the LP alone, but this is the first iterated version.
backlog.title: Exact LP polish of the final packing with iterated SLSQP

backlog.spec: For 40% of the time, optimise 16 free circles plus their mirror images across x=0.5, so the variables are 16 centres and radii. Constraints cover all 32 circles built from this. This halves the dimension and makes SLSQP much faster. Then desymmetrise the best result and polish it with a full 32-circle SLSQP for 200 iterations. Run the remaining time in the usual pool loop, seeding the pool with the polished results.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric search with symmetric SLSQP

backlog.spec: In SLSQP, replace the objective -sum(r) in the first 60 iterations with -sum(r) + 0.5*lambda*sum(r^2) using lambda=0.5, which encourages size variety. Then rerun with the true objective for up to 200 iterations. Both stages use the same constraints and start from the same x0. This regularizes the landscape early.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted objective with annealed exponent

backlog.spec: In the final 40% of the time, run restarts from the best pool packing. Pick a random disc of radius 0.25 in the square and re-randomise the centres of circles inside it by uniform noise within the disc. Set their radii to 0.03, relax the whole packing with a penalty L-BFGS-B at the current radii, then run SLSQP. Accept it into the pool via the diversity filter. This is a local region reshuffle, unlike the global jitter tried before.
backlog.title: Perturb-and-compress from the best with a hot restart schedule

backlog.spec: Set MAX_ITER to 400 and use tolerance ftol=1e-9 in SLSQP. Keep the relaxed starts and the pool of 5. Slots 11/32 show relaxed starts converge faster, so SLSQP is likely to stop before the cap. The extra iterations finish the slow active-set convergence that currently ends a run early, and the final sums become more accurate.
backlog.title: Lower-time-share multi-seed deterministic ensembles with bigger MAX_ITER

incumbent.description: Keep a pool of the 5 best packings and, 70% of the time once the pool has 2, start SLSQP from a vertical-cut crossover of two pool members, fixed to 32 circles by random removal or addition.

memo:
Helped: slot 0, a pool of the 5 best packings with SLSQP restarts from perturbed pool members (-2.9334, the only accepted change). Penalty-energy L-BFGS-B relaxation of fresh starts is the strongest signal: slot 11 gave -2.9396 on both of 2 runs, and slot 32 (noisy lattice or random starts, relaxed) also gave -2.9396/-2.9396. Slot 38 gave -2.9396/-2.9386. Diverse pool of 12 with the 1e-3 filter also helped (slot 18 -2.9386/-2.9349, slot 9 -2.9368), as did relocation (slot 29 -2.9396/-2.9360).
Did not help: schedule/time-fraction tuning (slots 1-6, within noise sd 0.0034), basin-hopping jitter (-2.9323), boundary-circle init (-2.9300), drop-and-resample (-2.9307), smallest-circle reinsertion (-2.9237), LP repair (-2.9297), multi-stage or reduced-constraint SLSQP (as low as -2.9044), analytic gradients (no change).
Next: adopt slot 11 as the base (-2.9396 replicated). Combine it with the pool of 12 and the 1e-3 filter, then add relocation. Avoid schedule tuning, large perturbations and repeating aborted ideas.
